text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - South Korea's Daehan Flour Mills Co Ltd bought 21,500 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat Tuesday from Mitsubishi Corp. It bought 5,000 tonnes of western white/soft white (ordinary) at $133.90 per tonne, FOB; 1,000 western white/soft white wheat (10 percent protein) at $134.65; 7,000 of hard red winter (HRW) wheat (11.5 percent protein) at $136.80 and 8,500 of dark northern spring wheat (14 percent protein), at $166.80. Shipment was for Sept 5-Oct 5 to Inchon.

CORN SALE - South Korean buyers group Top Margin Committee bought 52,500 tonnes of corn from Cargill. Arrival was for December 10 at Inchon. It paid $ 121.53 a tonne C&F if from the Pacific Northwest for Nov 11-30, $120.73 if from the U.S. Gulf for Oct 21-Nov 10. The seller may deliver China corn at $116.73.

CORN TENDERS - South Korea will invite tenders on Saturday to buy 50,000 tonnes of corn to be delivered to famine-threatened North Korea, the state run Agricultural and Fishery Marketing Corp said. Bids were due at 0300 GMT Saturday. Shipments will be made in 5,000 to 10,000 tonnes each during August to North Korea's port of Nampo.

SOYBEAN TENDER - South Korea's state-run Agricultural and Fishery Marketing Corp seeks on July 15 to buy 40,000 tonnes of No.1 soybeans. The total will be 20,000 tonnes for September 20 arrival at Inchon and 20,000 tonnes for arrival by October 20.
WHEAT TENDER - The CCC on July 9 will tender to buy 35,000 tonnes of hard red winter for donation to Tajikistan. Shipment was scheduled for July 23 to August 7.

RICE TENDER - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs will receive offers until July 23 to buy 24,000 tonnes of white rice for August delivery, a GEZA spokesman said. Results would be available on July 24.

VEGETABLE OIL TENDER - Egypt's state Holding Company for Food Industries on July 16 will seek 25,000 to 40,000 tonnes of cotton seed, sunflower seed and soybean oils for delivery in August. The tender includes 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes of crude sunflower seed oil and/or semi-refined cotton seed oil and/or American cottonseed oil PBSY 162 for arrival in the first half of August, 1997. - The same amounts and types of oil for second-half August arrival. Also, 5,000 to 10,000 tonnes of degummed soya bean oil second-half August arrival.

MARKET TALK - U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman confirmed Tuesday that the United States is considering renewing export subsidies for wheat flour and barley malt. But, in remarks to the Commodity Club, Glickman noted that market conditions did not yet justify renewing export subsidies for wheat and other bulk commodities.

- China's grain reserves stand at n all-time record high, Vice Premier Zhu Rongji said on Tuesday but added a call to officials to ensure payments to farmers at proper prices to maintain bumper harvests. China has reported a bumper summer harvest for the third consecutive year, resulting in a drop in grain prices in some places, the Xinhua news agency quoted Zhu as telling a conference on agriculture.

- USDA issued an authorization for Georgia to buy $20 million of U.S. wheat under Public Law 480, the agency said Tuesday. The authorization provides for about 95,000 tonnes of wheat grade U.S. No. 2 or better, except that durum shall grade U.S. No. 3 or better. The delivery period begins July 15 and ends on Dec. 31.
